stories.headline: Riksbank holds rate at 1.75% for fifth consecutive meeting amid Middle East uncertainty
stories.summary: Sweden's Riksbank kept its policy rate unchanged at 1.75% at the May 7 meeting, citing weak inflation (April CPIF at 0.8%, far below target) and subdued growth, while noting the Middle East war has increased upside inflation risks somewhat. In a notable shift, the bank dropped its previous forward guidance that rates would remain steady 'for some time to come,' signaling readiness to act in either direction.

stories.headline: Moderate Party holds election convention with German Chancellor Merz as guest; launches 'Fairer Sweden' campaign
stories.summary: Sweden's Moderate Party held its 'Sverigemöte' election convention in Stockholm on May 9-10, with German Chancellor Friedrich Merz attending as a high-profile guest speaker. Kristersson announced the party's headline election pledge of 5,000 SEK more per month for families, Merz reinforced NATO unity messaging and rebuked Slovakia's Fico for visiting Moscow, and the party launched its campaign slogan 'ett rättvisare Sverige' ('a fairer Sweden'). Separately on May 5, government and SD presented a joint review of the Tidö Agreement ahead of the September election.

stories.headline: SD breaks parliamentary pairing agreement, triggering riksdag voting crisis and ongoing political fallout
stories.summary: On April 29, Sweden Democrats sent two already-paired-off MPs to vote on a citizenship law, breaking a decades-old pairing convention and passing the measure. The act triggered a weekslong crisis: the Speaker convened emergency talks, a party leaders' debate was cancelled due to attendance demands, Åkesson accused Green Party of 'buying' independent MPs' votes, and multiple commentators likened the move to democratic norm erosion. The crisis remained unresolved through the analysis week with all 349 MPs required to attend votes.

stories.headline: Sweden establishes new civilian foreign intelligence agency UND, likened to Britain's MI6
stories.summary: On May 5, Foreign Minister Maria Malmer Stenergard announced Sweden will create a new civilian foreign intelligence service (Sveriges utrikes underrättelsetjänst, UND), described as Sweden's largest intelligence reform in decades. The agency, budgeted at 2.8 billion SEK, will begin operations January 1, 2027, and will partially absorb functions from military intelligence service MUST, working alongside Sapo and FRA. The decision was justified by intelligence failures ahead of Russia's 2022 Ukraine invasion.

stories.headline: Sweden and Ukraine advance Gripen fighter jet deal; defense ministers hold joint press conference
stories.summary: Ukraine's Defense Minister Mykhailo Fedorov visited Stockholm on May 7-8, meeting PM Kristersson, Defense Minister Pål Jonson, and the Saab Gripen manufacturer in Linköping. Fedorov announced Ukraine has a financing plan and predicted 'good news' within months on a Gripen E purchase; Jonson confirmed active negotiations on both Gripen E and C/D variants. Sweden also transferred airfield maintenance equipment to Ukraine. Separately, Jonson called Saudi Arabia's defense minister to discuss regional security.
